4982.d: To save, heal, preserve, rescue. From a primary sos; to save, i.e. Deliver or protect.

4396.d: A foreteller; by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet.

4367.d: (a) I instruct, command, (b) I appoint, assign. From pros and tasso; to arrange towards, i.e. enjoin.

4352.d: To fawn or crouch to, i.e. prostrate oneself in homage.

4863.d: To lead together, i.e. Collect or convene; specially, to entertain.

4254.d: To lead forward; intransitively, to precede (participle, previous).

4666.d: Myrrh. Apparently strengthened for muron; myrrh.

4471.d: Rama, a place in Ephraim, two hours north of Jerusalem. Of Hebrew origin; Rama, a place in Palestine.

4478.d: Rachel, younger wife of the patriarch Jacob. Of Hebrew origin; Rachel, the wife of Jacob.

4172.d: A city, the inhabitants of a city. Probably from the same as polemos, or perhaps from polus; a town.

4215.d: A river, torrent, stream. Probably from a derivative of the alternate of pino; a current, brook or freshet, i.e. Running water.

4491.d: A root, shoot, source; that which comes from the root, a descendent. Apparently a primary word; a |root|.

4442.d: Fire; the heat of the sun, lightning; fig: strife, trials; the eternal fire. A primary word; |fire|.

4621.d: Wheat, grain. Also plural irregular neuter sita of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat.

4058.d: A dove, pigeon. Of uncertain derivation; a pigeon.

4334.d: To approach, i.e. come near, visit, or worship, assent to.

4487.d: An utterance, ; by implication, a matter or topic; with a negative naught whatever.

4750.d: The mouth, speech, eloquence in speech, the point of a sword.

4419.d: An extremity, battlement, parapet, apex. Neuter of a presumed derivative of pterux; a winglet, i.e. extremity.

4219.d: When, at what time. From the base of pou and te; interrogative adverb, at what time.

4350.d: To strike at, i.e. Surge against; specially, to stub on, i.e. Trip up.

4228.d: The foot. A primary word; a |foot|.

4567.d: An adversary, Satan. Of Chaldee origin corresponding to ma'bad; the accuser, i.e. The devil.

4008.d: Over, on the other side, beyond. Apparently accusative case of an obsolete derivative of peiro; through, i.e. Across.

4653.d: Darkness; fig: spiritual darkness. From skotos; dimness, obscurity.

4639.d: |shade| or a shadow (darkness of error or an adumbration).

4043.d: To tread all around, i.e. Walk at large; figuratively, to live, deport oneself, follow.

4613.d: Simon. Of Hebrew origin; Simon, the name of nine Israelites.

4074.d: Peter, a Greek name meaning rock. Apparently a primary word; a rock; as a name, Petrus, an apostle.

4260.d: To go forward, advance. From pro and the base of basis; to walk forward, i.e. Advance.

4143.d: A ship, vessel, boat. From pleo; a sailer, i.e. Vessel.

4013.d: To lead or carry about (or around), go about, traverse. From peri and ago; to take around; reflexively, to walk around.

4864.d: An assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish |synagogue|; by analogy, a Christian church.

4947.d: Syria, a great Roman imperial province, united with Cilicia. Probably of Hebrew origin; Syria, a region of Asia.

4164.d: Various, of different colors, diverse, various. Of uncertain derivation; motley, i.e. Various in character.

4912.d: To hold together, i.e. To compress or arrest; figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy.

4583.d: To be a lunatic, be moonstruck, epileptic.

4434.d: Poor, destitute, spiritually poor, either in a good sense (humble devout persons) or bad.

4239.d: Mild, gentle. Apparently a primary word; mild, i.e. humble.

4253.d: |fore|, i.e. In front of, prior to.

4052.d: To superabound, be in excess, be superfluous; also to cause to superabound or excel.

4119.d: Or neuter pleion, or pleon comparative of polus; more in quantity, number, or quality; also the major portion.

4469.d: Empty, foolish. Of Chaldee origin; O empty one, i.e. Thou worthless.

4892.d: A council, tribunal; the Sanhedrin, the meeting place of the Sanhedrin.

4412.d: First, in the first place, before, formerly. Neuter of protos as adverb; firstly.

4624.d: To entrap, i.e. Trip up (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure).

4851.d: To bear together, i.e. to collect, or to conduce; especially advantage.

4983.d: Body, flesh; the body of the Church. From sozo; the body, used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively.

4202.d: Fornication, whoredom; met: idolatry. From porneuo; harlotry; figuratively, idolatry.

4053.d: Superabundant or superior; by implication, excessive; adverbially violently; neuter preeminence.

4474.d: To slap, strike, smite with the hand. From a derivative of a primary rhepo; to slap.

4600.d: The jawbone, cheek, jaw. Of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. the cheek or side of the face.

4762.d: Strengthened from the base of trope; to twist, i.e. Turn quite around or reverse.

4139.d: Near, nearby, a neighbor. Neuter of a derivative of pelas; close by; as noun, a neighbor, i.e. Fellow.

4336.d: To pray, pray for, offer prayer. From pros and euchomai; to pray to God, i.e. Supplicate, worship.

4337.d: To hold the mind towards, i.e. Pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to.

4537.d: To sound a trumpet. From salpigx; to trumpet, i.e. Sound a blast.

4113.d: A street, public square, broad way. Feminine of platus; a wide |plat| or |place|, i.e. Open square.

4180.d: Much-speaking, loquacity. From a compound of polus and logos; loquacity, i.e. Prolixity.

4594.d: Today, now. Neuter of a presumed compound of the article ho and hemera; on the day; generally, now.

4506.d: To rescue, deliver (from danger or destruction).

4659.d: Angry-visaged, i.e. Gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance.

4383.d: The front, i.e. The countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person.

4597.d: A moth. Apparently of Hebrew origin; a moth.

4652.d: Full of darkness, dark. From skotos; opaque, i.e. benighted.

4655.d: Darkness, either physical or moral. From the base of skia; shadiness, i.e. Obscurity.

4214.d: How much, how great, how many. From an absolute pos and hos; interrogative pronoun how much (plural) many).

4095.d: To drink, imbibe. A prolonged form of pio, which poo occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses; to imbibe.

4071.d: A bird, fowl. Neuter of a derivative of petomai; a flying animal, i.e. Bird.

4687.d: To sow, spread, scatter. Probably strengthened from spao; to scatter, i.e. Sow.

4369.d: To place (put) to, add; I do again. From pros and tithemi; to place additionally, i.e. Lay beside, annex, repeat.

4083.d: A cubit, about a foot and a half. Of uncertain affinity; the fore-arm, i.e. a cubit.

4459.d: Adverb from the base of pou; an interrogative particle of manner; in what way?; also as exclamation, how much!

4016.d: To throw all around, i.e. Invest.

4674.d: Yours, thy, thine. From su; thine.

4486.d: To rend, break asunder; I break forth (into speech); I throw or dash down.

4728.d: Narrow, strait. Probably from the base of histemi; narrow.

4439.d: A gate. Apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. The leaf or wing of a folding entrance.

4116.d: Broad, wide; subst: a street. From plasso; spread out |flat|, i.e. Broad.

4263.d: A sheep. Probably neuter of a presumed derivative of probaino; something that walks forward, i.e., a sheep.

4816.d: To collect, gather. From sun and lego in its original sense; to collect.

4718.d: A grape, cluster of grapes. Probably from the base of stephanos; a cluster of grapes.

4810.d: A (ripe) fig. Apparently a primary word; a fig.

4550.d: Rotten, useless, corrupt, depraved. From sepo; rotten, i.e. Worthless.

4395.d: To foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office.

4073.d: A rock, ledge, cliff, cave, stony ground. Feminine of the same as Petros; a rock.

4154.d: To blow, breathe, as the wind. A primary word; to breathe hard, i.e. Breeze.

4363.d: To fall towards, i.e. prostrate oneself, or to rush upon.

4431.d: A falling, a fall, ruin. From the alternate of pipto; a crash, i.e. Downfall.

4721.d: A flat roof of a house. Strengthened from a primary tegos; a roof.

4757.d: A soldier. From a presumed derivative of the same as stratia; a camper-out, i.e. A warrior.

4102.d: Faith, belief, trust, confidence; fidelity, faithfulness.

4100.d: To have faith, i.e. Credit; by implication, to entrust.

4445.d: To be sick with a fever. From pura; to be on fire, i.e., to have a fever.

4446.d: A fever, scorching heat. From puresso; inflamed, i.e. feverish.

4578.d: A shaking (as an earthquake); a storm. From seio; a commotion, i.e. a gale, an earthquake.

4217.d: Interrogatively, whatever, i.e. Of what possible sort.

4873.d: To recline at table with. From sun and anakeimai; to recline in company with.

4470.d: A piece of cloth, a remnant torn off. From rhegnumi; a |rag, | i.e. Piece of cloth.

4138.d: Repletion or completion, i.e. what fills, or what is filled.

4978.d: A rent, as in a garment; a division, dissention. From schizo; a split or gap, literally or figuratively.

4933.d: To keep closely together, i.e. to conserve; mentally, to remember.

4697.d: To feel compassion, have pity on, be moved.

4660.d: To flay, trouble, annoy, vex. Apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. to harass.

4496.d: To fling (see in ekteino), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit; by extension, to disperse.

4166.d: A shepherd; hence met: of the feeder, protector, and ruler of a flock of men. Of uncertain affinity; a shepherd.

4341.d: To call to myself, summon. Middle voice from pros and kaleo; to call toward oneself, i.e. Summon, invite.

4413.d: First, before, principal, most important. Contracted superlative of pro; foremost.

4541.d: A Samaritan. From Samareia; a Samarite, i.e. Inhabitant of Samaria.

4082.d: A sack, wallet for carrying provisions. Of uncertain affinity; a wallet or leather pouch for food.

4464.d: A rod, staff, staff of authority, scepter. From the base of rhapizo; a stick or wand.

4670.d: Sodom. Plural of Hebrew origin; Sodoma, a place in Palestine.

4765.d: A small bird, sparrow. Diminutive of strouthos; a little sparrow.

4453.d: To sell, exchange, barter. Probably ultimately from pelomai; to barter, i.e. To sell.

4531.d: To waver, i.e. Agitate, rock, topple or destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite.

4377.d: To sound towards, i.e. Address, exclaim, summon.

4678.d: Wisdom, insight, skill (human or divine), intelligence. From sophos; wisdom.

4719.d: A head of grain. From the base of histemi; a head of grain.

4286.d: A setting forth, i.e. proposal; specially, the show-bread as exposed before God.

4824.d: Neuter of a presumed derivative of sumboulos; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. The provincial assessors or lay-court.

4937.d: To crush completely, i.e. To shatter.

4570.d: (a) I extinguish, quench, (b) I suppress, thwart. A prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish.

4632.d: A vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband).

4650.d: To dissipate, i.e. put to flight, waste, be liberal.

4051.d: Abundance, overflow. From perisseuo; a surplus, or superabundance.

4592.d: Neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of semaino; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally.

4009.d: (a) a boundary, limit, extremity, (b) an end, conclusion. From the same as peran; an extremity.

4149.d: Wealth, i.e. money, possessions, or abundance, richness, valuable bestowment.

4846.d: To choke utterly, as weeds do plants; I crowd upon. From sun and pnigo; to strangle completely, i.e. to drown, or to crowd.

4885.d: To grow together. From sun and auzano; to increase together.

4615.d: Mustard (probably the shrub, not the herb). Perhaps from sinomai; mustard.

4094.d: A plate, platter, disc, dish. Apparently a form of plax; a plate.

4711.d: A plaited basket. From speiro; a hamper or lunch-receptacle.

4449.d: To be red, fire-colored. From purrhos; to redden.

4404.d: Early in the morning, at dawn. Adverb from pro; at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch.

4561.d: Flesh, body, human nature, materiality; kindred.

4355.d: (a) I take to myself, (b) I take aside, (c) I welcome. From pros and lambano; to take to oneself, i.e. Use, lead, admit.

4234.d: Practice, i.e. an act; by extension, a function.

4814.d: To talk with, discuss. From sun and laleo; to talk together, i.e. Converse.

4962.d: To roll or gather together. From sun and strepho; to twist together, i.e. Collect.

4868.d: To compare (settle) accounts, make a reckoning. From sun and airo; to make up together, i.e. to compute.

4169.d: Individualizing interrogative what sort of, or which one.

4476.d: A needle. From a primary rhapto; a needle.

4623.d: To keep silence, be silent, either voluntarily or involuntarily. From siope; to be dumb; figuratively, to be calm.

4808.d: A fig-tree. From sukon; a fig-tree.

4420.d: A wing, pinion. From a derivative of petomai; a wing.

4171.d: A war, battle, strife. From pelomai; warfare.

4654.d: To darken. From skotos; to obscure.

4167.d: A flock (of sheep or goats). Contraction from poimaino; a flock.

4351.d: To roll to, roll up against. From pros and kulioo; to roll towards, i.e. Block against.

4108.d: Roving, i.e. an impostor or misleader.

4106.d: Feminine of planos; objectively, fraudulence; subjectively, a straying from orthodoxy or piety.

4972.d: To seal, set a seal upon. From sphragis; to stamp for security or preservation; by implication, to keep secret, to attest.

4682.d: To convulse, throw into spasms. Prolongation from spairo; to mangle, i.e. Convluse with epilepsy.

4802.d: To seek together, discuss, dispute. From sun and zeteo; to investigate jointly, i.e. Discuss, controvert, cavil.

4017.d: To look around on, survey. From peri and blepo; to look all around.

4818.d: To be moved to grief by sympathy. From sun and lupeo; to afflict jointly, i.e. sorrow at someone.

4457.d: Hardness of heart, obtuseness. From poroo; stupidity or callousness.

4128.d: A multitude, crowd, great number, assemblage. From pletho; a fulness, i.e. A large number, throng, populace.

4142.d: (a little boat, hence) a boat. Neuter of a presumed derivative of ploion; a boat.

4342.d: To persist, persevere in, continue steadfast in; I wait upon.

4739.d: To stand fast, stand firm, persevere. From the perfect tense of histemi; to be stationary, i.e. to persevere.

4703.d: Seed for sowing. From speiro; a scattering, i.e. seed.

4403.d: The stern of a ship. Feminine of prumnus; the stern of a ship.

4344.d: A pillow or cushion. Neuter of a presumed compound of pros and kephale; something for the head, i.e. A cushion.

4993.d: To be of sound mind, be sober-minded, exercise self-control. From sophron; to be of sound mind, i.e. Sane, moderate.

4918.d: To press on all sides, crowd upon. From sun and thlibo; to compress, i.e. Crowd on all sides.

4511.d: A flowing, an issue. From rhoumai in the sense of its congener rheo; a flux.

4077.d: A fountain, spring, well, issue, flow. Probably from pegnumi; a fount, i.e. Source or supply.

4870.d: To accompany, follow together with. From sun and akoloutheo; to accompany.

4773.d: Akin to, related; subst: fellow countryman, kinsman. From sun and genos; a relative; by extension, a fellow countryman.

4547.d: A sandal. Neuter of a derivative of sandalon; a slipper or sole-pad.

4710.d: (a) speed, haste, (b) diligence, earnestness, enthusiasm. From speudo; |speed|, i.e. despatch, eagerness, earnestness.

4688.d: A body-guardsman; an executioner. Of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. Military scout (by extension) life-guardsman).

4936.d: To run (rush) together, run with. From sun and trecho; to rush together or headlong.

4849.d: A drinking party, festive company. Neuter of a derivative of the alternate of sumpino; a drinking-party, i.e. a room of guests.

4237.d: A company formed into divisions (like garden-beds). Perhaps from prason; a garden plot, i.e. a row.

4456.d: To harden, render callous, petrify. Apparently from poros; to petrify, i.e. to indurate.

4358.d: I anchor at a place. From pros and a derivative of the same as horme (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. land at.

4063.d: To run around. From peri and trecho; to run around, i.e. Traverse.

4064.d: To carry around; pass: To be driven to and fro. From peri and phero; to convey around, i.e. Transport hither and thither.

4435.d: The fist. From a primary pux; the clenched hand, i.e. with the fist.

4124.d: Covetousness, avarice, aggression, desire for advantage. From pleonektes; avarice, i.e. fraudulency, extortion.

4949.d: Feminine of a compound of Suros and the same as Phoinike; a Syro-phoenician woman, i.e. A female native of Phoenicia in Syria.

4429.d: To spit. A primary verb; to spit.

4727.d: To groan, expressing grief, anger, or desire. From stenos; to make in straits, i.e. to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly.

4744.d: To shine, glisten, flash, be radiant. Apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. Flash intensely.

4370.d: To run to. From pros and trecho; to run towards, i.e. Hasten to meet or join.

4952.d: To throw violently on the ground. From sun and sparasso; to rend completely, i.e. to convulse violently.
r: threw the boy into a convulsion

4029.d: To lie all around, i.e. Inclose, encircle, hamper.

4663.d: A gnawing worm; gnawing anguish. Of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm.

4848.d: To journey together; by implication, to assemble.

4347.d: To glue to, i.e. to adhere.

4819.d: To happen, occur, meet. From sun and the base of basis; to walk together, i.e. Concur.

4365.d: To come to, approach. From pros and poreuomai; to journey towards, i.e. Approach.

4319.d: To beg, ask earnestly, ask for in addition. From pros and aiteo; to ask repeatedly, i.e. Solicit.

4462.d: Or rhabbouni of Chaldee origin; corresponding to rhabbi.

4746.d: A bough, branch of a tree. From a primary steibo; a spread of loose materials for a couch, i.e. a bough of a tree so employed.

4907.d: A mental putting together, i.e. Intelligence or the intellect.

4749.d: A long robe, worn by the upper classes in the East. From stello; equipment, i.e., a |stole| or long-fitting gown.

4392.d: A pretext, an excuse. From a compound of pro and phaino; an outward showing, i.e. Pretext.

4931.d: To bring to an end, fulfill, accomplish. From sun and teleo; to complete entirely; generally, to execute.

4305.d: To be anxious beforehand, ponder beforehand. From pro and merimnao; to care in advance.

4185.d: Very costly, very precious, of great value. From polus and telos; extremely expensive.

4101.d: Genuine, pure (of ointment), trustworthy. From pistis; trustworthy, i.e. Genuine.

4301.d: To take in advance, i.e. eat before others have an opportunity; to anticipate, surprise.

4880.d: To die together with. From sun and apothnesko; to decease in company with, or, similarly to.

4953.d: A signal agreed upon. Neuter of a compound of sun and the base of semaino; a sign in common, i.e. Preconcerted signal.

4685.d: To draw (as a sword), pull. A primary verb; to draw.

4775.d: To sit with. From sun and kathemai; to seat oneself in company with.

4028.d: To cover up, cover round about, veil round, blindfold. From peri and kalupto; to cover all around, i.e. Entirely.

4475.d: A slap, blow on the cheek with the open hand. From rhapizo; a slap.

4259.d: A porch, court before a building, vestibule. Neuter of a presumed compound of pro and aule; a forecourt, i.e. Vestibule.

4955.d: A fellow insurgent. From a compound of sun and a derivative of stasis; a fellow-insurgent.

4714.d: A standing, i.e. position; by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy.

4779.d: To call together. From sun and kaleo; to convoke.

4209.d: The |purple| mussel, i.e. the red-blue color itself, and finally a garment dyed with it.

4669.d: To mingle with myrrh. From Smurna; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. Embitter.

4539.d: Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John, the apostles. Probably of Hebrew origin; Salome, an Israelitess.

4872.d: To go up with. From sun and anabaino; to ascend in company with.

4315.d: The day before the Sabbath. From pro and sabbaton; a fore-sabbath, i.e. The Sabbath-eve.

4327.d: To admit (figuratively) endurance); by implication, to await.

4225.d: Genitive case of an indefinite pronoun pos otherwise obsolete; as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. Nearly.

4903.d: To cooperate with, work together. From sunergos; to be a fellow-worker, i.e. Co-operate.

4135.d: To carry out fully, i.e. Completely assure, entirely accomplish.

4608.d: Intoxicating drink. Of Hebrew origin; an intoxicant, i.e. Intensely fermented liquor.

4246.d: An old man, an ambassador. From the same as presbuteros; an old man.

4032.d: To conceal, hide (by putting something around it). From peri and krupto; to conceal all around, i.e. Entirely.

4640.d: To leap (for joy), skip, bound. Akin to skairo; to jump, i.e. Sympathetically move.

4990.d: A savior, deliverer, preserver. From sozo; a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ.

4147.d: To become rich, be rich, abound in. From ploutizo; to be wealthy.

4040.d: Dwelling around; subst: a neighbor. From peri and oikos; housed around, i.e. Neighboring.

4796.d: To rejoice with, congratulate. From sun and chairo; to sympathize in gladness, congratulate.

4059.d: To cut around, circumcise. From peri and the base of tomoteros; to cut around, i.e. to circumcise.

4772.d: Kindred, family. From suggenes; relationship, i.e. relatives.

4093.d: A tablet for writing. Diminutive of pinax; a tablet.

4039.d: To dwell around, be neighboring to. From peri and oikeo; to reside around, i.e. Be a neighbor.

4991.d: Feminine of a derivative of soter as noun; rescue or safety.

4313.d: To precede, pass on before, go before. From pro and poreuomai; to precede.

4698.d: An intestine; figuratively, pity or sympathy.

4416.d: First-born, eldest. From protos and the alternate of tikto; first-born.

4683.d: To swathe, wrap in swaddling clothes. From sparganon; to swathe.

4034.d: To shine around. From peri and lampo; to illuminate all around, i.e. Invest with a halo.

4756.d: Feminine of a derivative of stratos; camp-likeness, i.e. An army, i.e. the angels, the celestial luminaries.

4692.d: To hasten, urge on, desire earnestly. Probably strengthened from pous; to |speed|, i.e. Urge on; by implication, to await eagerly.

4820.d: To combine, i.e. to converse, consult, dispute, to consider, to aid, to join, attack.

4826.d: Simeon or Simon. From the same as Simon; Symeon, the name of five Israelites.

4992.d: Saving, bringing salvation; subst: salvation. Neuter of the same as soteria as noun; defender or defence.

4501.d: A sword, scimitar; fig: war, piercing grief. Probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. A long and broad cutlass.

4398.d: A prophetess. Feminine of prophetes; a female foreteller or an inspired woman.

4923.d: A company traveling together, a caravan. From a compound of sun and hodos; companionship on a journey, i.e., a caravan.

4298.d: To drive forward, i.e. to advance.

4003.d: The fifteenth. From pente and kai and dekatos; five and tenth.

4194.d: Pontius. Of Latin origin; apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman.

4646.d: Crooked, perverse, unfair, curved, tortuous. From the base of skelos; warped, i.e. Winding; figuratively, perverse.

4238.d: To do, perform, accomplish; be in any condition, i.e. I fare; I exact, require.

4754.d: To wage war, fight, serve as a soldier; fig: of the warring lusts against the soul.

4811.d: To be a fig-informer, |sycophant|, i.e. to defraud.

4984.d: Bodily, corporeal. From soma; corporeal or physical.

4584.d: Semein, an ancestor of Jesus. Of Hebrew origin; Semei, an Israelite.

4488.d: Rhesa, an ancestor of Jesus. Probably of Hebrew origin; Resa, an Israelite.

4527.d: Sala, the name of two of the ancestors of Jesus. Of Hebrew origin; Sala, a patriarch.

4562.d: Serug, an ancestor of Jesus. Of Hebrew origin; Saruch, a patriarch.

4466.d: Ragau (or Reu), an ancestor of Jesus. Of Hebrew origin; Ragau, a patriarch.

4590.d: Shem, a son of Noah. Of Hebrew origin; Sem, a patriarch.

4589.d: Seth, third son of Adam. Of Hebrew origin; Seth, a patriarch.

4743.d: A moment, point of time, an instant. Feminine of stigma; a point of time, i.e. An instant.

4428.d: To fold, roll up (as a scroll). Probably akin to petannumi; to fold, i.e. Furl a scroll.

4558.d: Zarephath, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia. Of Hebrew origin; Sarepta, a place in Palestine.

4606.d: Sidonian, inhabitant of Sidon. From Sidon; a Sidonian, i.e. Inhabitant of Sidon.

4948.d: Syrian, belonging to Syria. From the same as Suria; a Syran, a native of Syria.

4150.d: To wash. A prolonged form of an obsolete pluo; to |plunge|, i.e. Launder clothing.

4788.d: To enclose, shut in, make subject to. From sun and kleio; to shut together, i.e. Include or embrace in a common subjection to.

4023.d: To hold all around, i.e. Include, clasp.

4437.d: Frequent, often, much. From the same as skenopoios; clasped, i.e. frequent; neuter plural frequently.

4273.d: A betrayer, traitor. From prodidomi (the enemy's) hands); a surrender.

4085.d: To press down, press together, as in a measure. Another form for piazo; to pack.

4393.d: To bring forth, produce. From pro and phero; to bear forward, i.e. Produce.

4626.d: To dig, excavate. Apparently a primary verb; to dig.

4132.d: A flood. Prolonged from pletho; flood-tide, i.e. a freshet.

4366.d: To dash against, as waves. From pros and rhegnumi; to tear towards, i.e. Burst upon.

4485.d: What is broken, a ruin. From rhegnumi; something torn, i.e. A fragment.

4709.d: Diligently, earnestly, zealously. Adverb from spoudaios; earnestly, promptly.

4673.d: A bier, an open coffin. Probably akin to the base of soreuo; a funereal receptacle, i.e. a bier.

4001.d: Five hundred. From pente and hekaton; five hundred.

4677.d: Susannah, a woman of the retinue of Jesus. Of Hebrew origin; lily; Susannah, an Israelitess.

4896.d: To come together. From sun and eimi; to assemble.

4855.d: To grow at the same time. From sun and phuo; passive, to grow jointly.

4940.d: To meet with, come to, fall in with. From sun and tugchano; to chance together, i.e. Meet with.

4126.d: Another form for pleuo; which is used as an alternate in certain tenses; probably a form of pluno; to pass in a vessel.

4845.d: To fill completely; pass: To be completed. From sun and pleroo; to implenish completely, i.e. to swamp, or to accomplish.

4884.d: To seize, drag by force. From sun and harpazo; to snatch together, i.e. Seize.

4321.d: To spend in addition. From pros and analisko; to expend further.

4895.d: To be with, come together with. From sun and eimi; to be in company with, i.e. Present at the time.

4921.d: To place together, commend, prove, exhibit; instrans: I stand with; To be composed of, cohere.

4601.d: Intrans: I am silent, keep silence; trans: I keep secret; pass: I am kept secret. From sige; to keep silent.

4876.d: To meet, encounter, fall in with. From sun and a derivative of anti; to meet with; figuratively, to occur.

4317.d: To lead towards, i.e. to conduct near, or to approach.

4741.d: To set fast, i.e. to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or to confirm.

4651.d: A scorpion. Probably from an obsolete skerpo; a |scorpion|.

4045.d: To fall into something that is all around, i.e. Light among or upon, be surrounded with.

4127.d: A blow, stripe, wound; an affliction, plague. From plesso; a stroke; by implication, a wound; figuratively, a calamity.

4795.d: A coincidence, accident, chance. From a comparative of sun and kureo; concurrence, i.e. Accident.

4325.d: To spend in addition. From pros and dapanao; to expend additionally.

4049.d: To distract, trouble greatly. From peri and spao; to drag all around, i.e. to distract.

4878.d: To take hold of opposite together, i.e. Co-operate.

4661.d: Spoil taken from a foe. Neuter from skullo; something stripped, i.e. Booty.

4648.d: To look at, regard attentively, take heed, beware, consider. From skopos; to take aim at, i.e. regard.

4076.d: Rue, a plant used for flavoring or garnishing food. From pegnumi; rue.

4379.d: To touch lightly. From pros and psauo; to impinge, i.e. Lay a finger on.

4909.d: To think well of in common, i.e. Assent to, feel gratified with.

4780.d: To conceal closely, cover up wholly. From sun and kalupto; to conceal altogether.

4168.d: A little flock. Neuter of a presumed derivative of poimne; a flock, i.e. group.

4024.d: To gird all around, i.e. to fasten on one's belt.

4620.d: A measured portion of grain or food. From sitos and metron; a grain-measure, i.e. ration.

4233.d: An officer employed to execute judicial sentences. From a derivative of prasso; a practiser, i.e., an official collector.

4611.d: Siloam, a spring within the walls, in the south-east corner of Jerusalem. Of Hebrew origin; Siloam, a pool of Jerusalem.

4794.d: To be bowed together, bent double. From sun and kupto; to stoop altogether, i.e. Be completely overcome by.

4197.d: A journey, pursuit, undertaking, progress. From poreuomai; travel; figuratively proceedings, i.e. Career.

4320.d: To go up to, come up to, go up further. From pros and anabaino; to ascend farther, i.e. Be promoted (more honorable) seat).

4242.d: An embassy, delegation, eldership. From presbeuo; seniority, i.e. an embassy.

4906.d: To eat with. From sun and esthio; to take food in company with.

4177.d: A citizen, fellow-citizen. From polis; a townsman.

4618.d: Fattened, fatted. From a derivative of sitos; grain-fed, i.e. Fattened.

4858.d: Harmony of instruments, music. From sumphonos; unison of sound, i.e. A concert of instruments.

4807.d: A sycamore tree, black mulberry tree. Of Hebrew origin in imitation of sukomoraia; a sycamore-fig tree.

4540.d: Samaria, a city and region of Palestine.

4207.d: From far, or at a distance, i.e. Distantly.

4046.d: To acquire, earn, purchase, make my own, preserve alive.

4738.d: The breast, chest. From histemi; the bosom, i.e. Chest.

4179.d: Many times more, manifold. From polus and probably a derivative of pleko; manifold, i.e. very much more.

4390.d: To run before, outrun, run in advance. From pro and trecho; to run forward, i.e. Outstrip, precede.

4809.d: A sycamore tree. From sukon and moron; the |sycamore|-fig tree.

4231.d: To transact business, trade. From pragma; to busy oneself with, i.e. To trade.

4333.d: To gain, produce in addition. From pros and ergazomai; to work additionally, i.e. acquire besides.

4676.d: A handkerchief, napkin. Of Latin origin; a sudarium, i.e. Towel.

4455.d: At any time, ever. From po and pote; at any time, i.e. at no time.

4033.d: To encircle, surround, encompass. From peri and kukloo; to encircle all around, i.e. Blockade completely.

4817.d: To reason, reckon with myself, consider. From sun and logizomai; to reckon together, i.e. Deliberate.

4422.d: To terrify, scare, strike with panic. Probably akin to the alternate of pipto or to petomai; to scare.

4304.d: To meditate beforehand, prepare, get up, premeditate. From pro and meletao; to premeditate.

4760.d: An encamped army. From the base of stratia and the same as pedinos; a camping-ground, i.e. a body of troops.

4928.d: Distress, anguish, anxiety. From sunecho; restraint, i.e. anxiety.

4535.d: The tossing of the sea in a tempest; agitation, rolling. Probably from the base of saino; a vibration, i.e., billow.

4329.d: Expectation, waiting. From prosdokao; apprehension; by implication, infliction anticipated.

4261.d: To throw forward, i.e. Push to the front, germinate.

4755.d: A general, i.e. a governor, the chief of the temple-wardens.

4934.d: Mid. and pass: To make a compact (agreement) with (together), covenant with, agree.

4617.d: To sift, prove by trials, winnow. From sinion; to riddle.

4218.d: At one time or other, at some time, formerly. From the base of pou and te; indefinite adverb, at some time, ever.

4776.d: To cause to sit down with, sit down together. From sun and kathizo; to give a seat in company with.

4244.d: Neuter of a presumed derivative of presbuteros; the order of elders, i.e., Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian |presbytery|.

4391.d: To have been already, have been previously. From pro and huparcho; to exist before, i.e. to be or do something previously.

4836.d: To be present together, i.e. To convene; by implication, to appear in aid.

4784.d: To give a vote with, assent to. Mid from sun and katatithemi; to deposit in company with, i.e. to accord with.

4364.d: To pretend, regard, make a show of. Middle voice from pros and poieo; to do forward for oneself, i.e. Pretend.

4867.d: To gather together, assemble. From sun and athroizo; to convene.

4637.d: To dwell as in a tent, encamp, have my tabernacle. From skenos; to tent or encamp, i.e. to occupy or, to reside.

4979.d: A cord, rope. Diminutive of schoinos; a rushlet, i.e. Grass-withe or tie.

4530.d: Salim -- a place in Palestine. Probably from the same as saleuo; Salim, a place in Palestine.

4965.d: Sychar, a city of Samaria. Of Hebrew origin; Sychar, a place in Palestine.

4542.d: A Samaritan woman. Feminine of Samareites; a Samaritess, i.e. Woman of Samaria.

4798.d: To have dealings with. From sun and chraomai; to use jointly, i.e. to hold intercourse in common.

4353.d: A worshipper. From proskuneo; an adorer.

4262.d: Pertaining to sheep. From probaton; relating to sheep, i.e. through which they were led into Jerusalem.

4745.d: A colonnade, portico. Probably from histemi; a colonnade or interior piazza.

4897.d: To enter together with, embark with. From sun and eiserchomai; to enter in company with.

4213.d: Drinking, drink, beverage. From the alternate of pino; a drinking, i.e. a draught.

4386.d: Formerly, before. Neuter of proteros as adverb; previously.

4220.d: Which of two, whether. Neuter of a comparative of the base of pou; interrogative as adverb, which, i.e. Is it this or that.

4084.d: To squeeze, i.e. Seize (press), or officially (arrest), or in hunting (capture).

4482.d: To flow, overflow with. A primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form rheuo is used to flow.

4081.d: Clay, mud. Perhaps a primary word; clay.

4827.d: A fellow disciple. From a compound of sun and manthano; a co-learner.

4026.d: To stand all around, i.e. to be a bystander, or to keep away from.

4019.d: To bind (tie) around. Peri and deo; to bind around one, i.e. Enwrap.

4514.d: Roman; subst: a Roman citizen. From Rhome; Romaean, i.e. Roman.

4591.d: To signify, indicate, give a sign, make known. From sema; to indicate.

4418.d: The heel. Of uncertain derivation; the heel.

4914.d: A custom, habit, practice. From a compound of sun and ethos; mutual habituation, i.e. Usage.

4210.d: Purple. From porphura; purpureal, i.e. Bluish red.

4515.d: In the Latin language. Adverb from a presumed derivative of Rhome; Romaistically, i.e. In the Latin language.

4628.d: The leg (from the hip downwards). Apparently from skello; the leg.

4125.d: The side of the body. Of uncertain affinity; a rib, i.e. side.

4371.d: Neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of pros and phago; something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. A relish.

4951.d: To draw, drag, force away. Probably akin to haireomai; to trail.

4871.d: To be assembled together with. From sun and halizo; to accumulate, i.e. Convene.

4037.d: To wait for, await. From peri and meno; to stay around, i.e. Await.

4277.d: To say previously, predict, proclaim, foretell. From pro and epo; to say already, to predict.

4248.d: Falling headlong, prone. From pro; leaning forward, i.e. Head foremost.

4785.d: To be voted or classed with. From sun and a compound of kata and psephizo; to count down in company with, i.e. Enroll among.

4005.d: Feminine of the ordinal of pentekonta; fiftieth from Passover, i.e. The festival of |Pentecost|.

4157.d: (a) breath, (b) gust, breeze, wind. From pneo; respiration, a breeze.

4797.d: Or sugchuno from sun and cheo or its alternate; to commingle promiscuously, i.e. to throw into disorder, to perplex.

4195.d: A sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor.

4268.d: Foreknowledge, previous determination. From proginosko; forethought.

4362.d: To fasten to, applied to Christ's being fastened to the cross. From pros and pegnumi; to fasten to, i.e., to impale.

4308.d: To behold in advance, i.e. to notice previously, or to keep in view.

4974.d: The ankle bone. Neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as sphaira; the ankle.

4732.d: To strengthen, confirm, establish, settle. From stereos; to solidify, i.e. Confirm.

4293.d: To announce beforehand, promise, predict. From pro and kataggello; to anounce beforehand, i.e. Predict, promise.

4400.d: To appoint, choose, elect, take into hand.

4545.d: Samuel, a Hebrew prophet. Of Hebrew origin; Samuel, an Israelite.

4324.d: To utter additional threats. From pros and apeileo; to menace additionally.

4309.d: To foreordain, predetermine, mark out beforehand. From pro and horizo; to limit in advance, i.e. predetermine.

4551.d: Sapphira, wife of Ananias, an early Christian. Feminine of sappheiros; Sapphire, an Israelitess.

4894.d: To know, consider, be privy to.

4958.d: To contract, shorten, wrap around, swathe. From sun and stello; to send together, i.e. Enwrap, contract.

4038.d: Round about, neighboring. Adverb from peri; all around, i.e. circumjacent.

4742.d: A mark or brand. From a primary stizo; a mark incised or punched, i.e. scar of service.

4276.d: To hope before, be the first to hope. From pro and elpizo; to hope in advance of other confirmation.

4047.d: Acquiring, obtaining, possessing, possession, ownership. From peripoieomai; acquisition; by extension, preservation.

4806.d: To make alive together with. From sun and zoopoieo; to reanimate.

4891.d: To raise along with. From sun and egeiro; to rouse in company with, i.e. to revivify in resemblance to.
r: God raised us up with Christ

4847.d: A fellow citizen. From sun and polites; a native of the same town, i.e. co-religionist.

4883.d: To render close-jointed together, i.e. Organize compactly.

4925.d: To build together with. From sun and oikodomeo; to construct, i.e. to compose.

4954.d: Of a joint body, i.e. a fellow-member of the Christian community.

4830.d: Jointly partaking. From sun and metochos; a co-participant.

4182.d: Much varied, manifold. From polus and poikilos; much variegated, i.e. Multifarious.

4492.d: To cause to take root; met: I plant, fix firmly, establish. From rhiza; to root.

4656.d: (lit. or met.) I darken. From skotos; to obscure or blind.

4790.d: To share in company with, i.e. Co-participate in.

4696.d: A spot, fault, stain, blemish. Of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. defect, disgrace.

4512.d: A wrinkle; fig: a spiritual defect, flaw. From rhoumai; a fold, i.e. A wrinkle.

4030.d: A helmet. Feminine of a compound of peri and kephale; encirclement of the head, i.e. A helmet.

4297.d: Progress, advancement. From prokopto; progress, i.e. Advancement.

4866.d: To wrestle in company with, i.e. to seek jointly.

4426.d: To frighten, terrify. From a presumed derivative of ptuo; to frighten.

4689.d: To pour out as a libation. Apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. to devote.
r: being poured out like a drink offering

4961.d: A fellow soldier (in the Christian faith). From sun and stratiotes; a co-campaigner, i.e. an associate in Christian toil.

4708.d: More earnestly, diligently, zealously. Adverb from spoudaioteros; more speedily, i.e. Sooner than otherwise.

4657.d: Refuse, dregs, dung. Neuter of a presumed derivative of eis and kuon and ballo; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. Refuse.

4833.d: To bring to the same form with, conform. From summorphos; to render like, i.e. to assimilate.

4649.d: Perhaps akin to skapto through the idea of concealment; compare skepasma); a watch, i.e. a goal.

4831.d: A joint imitator. From a presumed compound of sun and mimeomai; a co-imitator, i.e. Fellow votary.

4175.d: A state, commonwealth. From politeuomai; a community, i.e. citizenship.

4941.d: Syntyche, a woman member of the church at Philippi. From suntugchano; an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female.

4805.d: Co-yoked, i.e. as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian.

4586.d: Venerable, honorable, grave, serious, dignified. From sebomai; venerable, i.e. Honorable.

4375.d: Pleasing, acceptable, grateful. From a presumed compound of pros and phileo; friendly towards, i.e. Acceptable.

4257.d: To hear beforehand. From pro and akouo; to hear already, i.e. Anticipate.

4409.d: To have preeminence, be chief, be first. From protos; to be first.

4136.d: Full assurance, conviction, confidence. From plerophoreo; entire confidence.

4086.d: Persuasive speech. From a compound of a derivative of peitho and logos; persuasive language.

4733.d: Firmness, steadfastness, constancy. From stereoo; something established, i.e. confirmation.

4812.d: To plunder, lead captive; met: I make victim by fraud. From the base of sulao and ago; to lead away as booty, i.e. seduce.

4985.d: Bodily, corporeally, belonging to the body. Adverb from somatikos; corporeally or physically.

4338.d: To fasten with nails, nail to. From pros and a derivative of helos; to peg to, i.e. Spike fast.

4140.d: Satisfaction, indulgence. From a presumed derivative of pletho; a filling up, i.e. gratification.

4658.d: A Scythian, as typical of the uncivilized. Probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. a savage.

4146.d: Richly, abundantly. Adverb from plousios; copiously.

4087.d: To make bitter, embitter; pass: I grow angry or harsh. From pikros; to embitter.

4192.d: (a) labor, toil, (b) pain, anguish, distress, suffering. From the base of penes; toil, i.e. anguish.

4310.d: To suffer previously. From pro and pascho; to undergo hardship previously.

4853.d: A co-tribesman, i.e. Native of the same country.

4525.d: To fawn upon, flatter, beguile; pass: To be perturbed. Akin to seio; to wag, i.e. to shake.

4035.d: To leave behind; pass: To be left behind, remain, survive. From peri and leipo; to leave all around, i.e. survive.

4020.d: To overdo, be a busybody, waste my labor about (a thing). From peri and ergazomai; to work all around, i.e. Bustle about.

4593.d: To note, mark for myself. From semeion; to distinguish, i.e. Mark.

4587.d: Dignity, honor, gravity, seriousness. From semnos; venerableness, i.e. Probity.

4117.d: Braided hair, anything interwoven. From pleko; a plait.

4131.d: A striker, contentious person, brawler. From plesso; a smiter, i.e. Pugnacious.

4490.d: Expressly, explicitly, in so many words. Adverb from a derivative of rheo; out-spokenly, i.e. Distinctly.

4269.d: An ancestor. From proginomai; an ancestor, parent.

4684.d: To live extravagantly, luxuriously; To be wanton. From spatale; to be voluptuous.

4299.d: A prejudgment, prejudice, partiality, preference. From a compound of pro and krino; a prejudgment, i.e. Prepossession.

4751.d: The stomach. From stoma; an orifice, i.e., the |stomach|.

4271.d: Manifest to all, evident, very clear. From pro and delos; plain before all men, i.e. Obvious.

4200.d: A source of gain, livelihood. From a derivative of poros; furnishing, i.e. money-getting.

4629.d: Clothing, a covering, raiment. From a derivative of skepas; clothing.

4044.d: To put on a spit; met: I pierce, wound deeply. From peri and the base of peran; to penetrate entirely, i.e. Transfix.

4995.d: Self-control, self-discipline, prudence. From sophronizo; discipline, i.e. Self-control.

4777.d: To suffer hardships together with. From sun and kakopatheo; to suffer hardship in company with.

4230.d: A business, an occupation, affair, transaction. From pragmateuomai; a transaction, i.e. Negotiation.

4758.d: To collect an army, enlist troops. From a compound of the base of stratia and lego; to gather as a warrior, i.e. Enlist in the army.

4737.d: To crown, adorn, decorate. From stephanos; to adorn with an honorary wreath.

4731.d: Solid, firm, steadfast. From histemi; stiff, i.e. Solid, stable.

4104.d: To convince, establish, give assurance to; pass: To be assured of. From pistos; to assure.

4679.d: To render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form |sophisms|, i.e. Continue plausible error.

4227.d: Pudens, a Christian man in Rome. Of Latin origin; modest; Pudes, a Christian.

4247.d: An old woman. Feminine of presbutes; an old woman.

4994.d: To make sober-minded, admonish, control. From sophron; to make of sound mind, i.e. to discipline or correct.

4996.d: Soberly, with moderation, prudently. Adverb from sophron; with sound mind, i.e. Moderately.

4065.d: To look down upon, despise. From peri and phroneo; to think beyond, i.e. Depreciate.

4767.d: Hateful, detestable, disgusting. From a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary stugo; hated, i.e. Odious.

4359.d: To owe besides (in addition). From pros and opheilo; to be indebted additionally.

4181.d: Adverb from a compound of polus and meros; in many portions, i.e. Variously as to time and agency.

4187.d: In many ways. Adverb from a compound of polus and tropos; in many ways, i.e. Variously as to method or form.

4901.d: To unite in bearing witness, sanction. From sun and epimartureo; to testify further jointly, i.e. Unite in adding evidence.

4360.d: To be displeased or offended with. From pros and a form of ochtheo; to feel indignant at.

4520.d: A keeping of the Sabbath, a Sabbath rest. From a derivative of sabbaton; a |sabbatism|, i.e. the repose of Christianity.

4834.d: To sympathize with, have compassion on. From sumpathes; to feel |sympathy| with, i.e. to commiserate.

4316.d: To address by name, designate, accost. From pros and a derivative of agora; to address, i.e. Salute by name.

4274.d: A precursor, forerunner, advance guard. From the alternate of protrecho; a runner ahead, i.e. Scout.

4532.d: Salem, doubtless identical with Jerusalem. Of Hebrew origin; Salem, a place in Palestine.

4078.d: To fasten, pitch a tent. A prolonged form of a primary verb; to fix, i.e. to set up.

4713.d: A jar or vase. From the base of histemi; a jar or earthen tank.

4472.d: To sprinkle, cleanse ceremonially by sprinkling. From a derivative of rhaino; to render besprinkled, i.e. Asperse.

4778.d: To suffer ill-treatment with. From sun and kakoucheo; to maltreat in company with, i.e. endure persecution together.

4378.d: A pouring upon, an effusion, a sprinkling. From a comparative of pros and cheo; a shedding forth, i.e. Affusion.

4460.d: Rahab, a Canaanitess, who rescued the Hebrew spies at Jericho. Of Hebrew origin; Raab, a Canaanitess.

4881.d: To perish along with. From sun and apollumi; to destroy in company with.

4546.d: Samson, one of the Judges of Israel. Of Hebrew origin; Sampson, an Israelite.

4249.d: To saw, saw through. A strengthened form of a primary prio; to saw in two.

4265.d: To provide, foresee. From pro and blepo; to look out beforehand, i.e. Furnish in advance.

4415.d: The birthright, the rights of the first-born. From prototokos; primogeniture.

4887.d: To bind with, i.e. be a fellow-prisoner.

4494.d: To toss to and fro, fan, blow. From a derivative of rhipto; to breeze up, i.e. to agitate.

4507.d: Filth, pollution, defilement. From rhuparos; dirtiness.

4162.d: A doing, making, performance. From poieo; action, i.e. Performance.

4508.d: Filthy, defiled, dirty. From rhupos; dirty, i.e. cheap or shabby; morally, wicked.

4380.d: To favor specially, show partiality. From prosopoleptes; to favor an individual, i.e. Show partiality.

4695.d: To defile, spot, stain, soil. From spilos; to stain or soil.

4089.d: Bitter, acrid, malignant. Perhaps from pegnumi; sharp, i.e. Acrid.

4170.d: To make war, contend, fight, battle. From polemos; to be in warfare, i.e. To battle: -fight, war.

4595.d: To cause to rot, make corrupt. Apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. perish.

4598.d: Moth-eaten. From ses and a derivative of bibrosko; moth-eaten.

4406.d: Dawning, early. From proi; dawning, i.e. autumnal.

4184.d: Very compassionate, of great mercy. From polus and splagchnon; extremely compassionate.

4303.d: To predict, testify or protest beforehand. From pro and marturomai; to be a witness in advance i.e. Predict.

4701.d: Seed sown, a sowing. From speiro; a sowing, i.e. parentage.

4025.d: A putting around or on (as of ornaments). From peritithemi; a putting all around, i.e. Decorating oneself with.

4423.d: Terror, consternation, dismay. From ptoeo; alarm.

4924.d: To dwell with, live in wedlock with. From sun and oikeo; to reside together.

4835.d: Sympathizing, compassionate. From sumpascho; having a fellow-feeling, i.e. mutually commiserative.

4509.d: Filth, filthiness, dirt, squalor. Of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. depravity.

4224.d: A drinking, carousing. From the alternate of pino; a drinking-bout or carousal.

4451.d: A burning, trial, fiery test. From puroo; ignition, i.e., smelting.

4850.d: A fellow elder. From sun and presbuteros; a co-presbyter.

4290.d: Readily, eagerly, with a ready mind, cheerfully. Adverb from prothumos; with alacrity.

4599.d: To strengthen. From sthenos; to strengthen, i.e. confirm.

4899.d: Fellow-elect, fellow-chosen. From a compound of sun and eklegomai; chosen in company with, i.e. Co-elect.

4112.d: Formed, molded; fig: feigned, made up, counterfeit. From plasso; moulded, i.e. artificial or fictitious.

4577.d: A chain. Probably from suro through its congener eiro; a chain.

4500.d: With a great noise, with a rushing sound. Adverb from a derivative of rhoizos; whizzingly, i.e. With a crash.

4761.d: To wrench, i.e., to torture, but only figuratively, to pervert.

4969.d: To slay, kill by violence, slaughter, wound mortally. A primary verb; to butcher or to slaughter, or, to maim.

4694.d: A hidden rock; fig: a flaw, stigma. Of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea.

4107.d: A wanderer. From planos; a rover, i.e. an erratic teacher.

4667.d: Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia. The same as smurna; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor.

4010.d: Pergamum, an important city of the Roman province Asia. From purgos; fortified; Pergamus, a place in Asia Minor.

4554.d: Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia. Plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor.

4158.d: Reaching to the feet (of a garment). From pous and another element of uncertain affinity; a dress reaching the ankles.

4407.d: Belonging to the morning, early. From proi; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. Matutinal.

4556.d: Carnelian, a precious stone. Properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian, i.e. the gem so called.

4664.d: Made of emerald, emerald-green. From smaragdos; consisting of emerald.

4072.d: To fly. Or prolongation petaomai, or contracted ptaomai middle voice of a primary verb; to fly.

4502.d: Reuben, eldest son of the patriarch Jacob and founder of a tribe. Of Hebrew origin; Ruben, an Israelite.

4141.d: To strike, smite. Apparently another form of plasso; to pound, i.e. to inflict with.

4447.d: Fiery, glittering. From pura; fiery, i.e. flaming.

4216.d: Carried away by a stream. From potamos and a derivative of phoreo; river-borne, i.e. Overwhelmed by a stream.

4764.d: Wantonness, luxury. Akin to stereos; a |straining|, |strenuousness| or |strength|, i.e. luxury.

4763.d: To live luxuriously, revel, riot. From a presumed derivative of strenos; to be luxurious.

4596.d: Silken, silk. From Ser; Seric, i.e. Silken.

4585.d: The finest wheaten flour. Probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour.

4480.d: A chariot. Of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. Four-wheeled carriage.

4538.d: A trumpeter. From salpizo; a trumpeter.

4552.d: A sapphire. Of Hebrew origin; a |sapphire| or lapis-lazuli gem.

4665.d: An emerald. Of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called.

4557.d: A |sardonyx|, i.e. The gem so called.

4510.d: To be filthy; hence (morally): To be stained with sin. From rhupos; to soil, i.e. to become dirty.
